To assemble a sample, RiboPilot compares its reads with known ribosomal
sequences from a reference database of related organisms. A new project has no
usable database until you build one in the app's **Reference** step. You do not 
need to find or format any sequences yourself, and a database can be reused by every
later project on that group.

# The Reference step

The Reference step comes between the **Taxonomy** and **Assemble** steps. Set
up a database for every group before you assemble.

After resolving the sample taxonomy, open the Reference step and press
**Propose groups**. RiboPilot looks at each sample's lineage and groups samples
that can share one reference database. RiboPilot picks the narrowest group
containing your samples that contains at least at least 1,000 GenBank rDNA
records. Samples from very different parts of the tree end up in 
different groups, each with its own reference database.

After defining groups, the Reference page automatically switches from a 
samples table to a groups table. Each row is one proposed group. The **Status** column says where that group
stands ("Needs a database", "Building", "Ready", "Build failed", or "Left on
current database"), and the rest of the row shows the clade, how many of your
samples it covers, and how many GenBank records were found.

## Setting a group up

The link at the right-hand end of each row says what that group needs: **Set up
database**, **Try again**, or **Change**. Click it and you are offered four
choices:

- **Download sequences from GenBank.** The normal choice. Opens a run window, 
  then press **Run from App** to download the database. When the build
  finishes, RiboPilot points the group's unlocked samples at the new database.
  A database that already exists in your reference folder is automatically used, 
  not rebuilt.
- **Use a database I already have.** Points the group at a database built
  earlier, in this project or by someone else sharing the reference folder.
- **Change which clade this group uses.** Lists the group's lineage from the
  broadest rank to the narrowest. Pick another rank to widen or narrow the
  group, or search for another clade. If some samples in the group are not contained
  in the clade you select, they are split off into a different group. 
  Clicking the group's **Clade** cell opens the same window.
- **Leave these samples on their current database.** Nothing is built. Use it
  only when you have already set a database in these samples' **Assembly
  Options** yourself.

To handle several groups at once, tick their rows first, then click the link on
any one of them. The "change clade" option is offered only for a single group.

If you press **Update** in the Assemble step while some groups have no
database, RiboPilot warns you but goes ahead, and those samples fail.

# The reference folder

Built databases live in a **reference folder** that can be shared across projects.
You can set the location of the reference folder using the **Settings** button
(which also lets you adjust the minimum and maximum record counts the grouping step uses).
Or you can set the reference folder when you create a project.

```r
RiboPilot::new_project(
  path       = "~/my_project",
  mapping_fn = "~/my_samples.csv",
  data_path  = "~/my_reads",
  ref_dir    = "~/ribopilot_refs"
)
```

If you do not set a folder, RiboPilot uses a folder in your home directory. 
`RiboPilot::ribopilot_ref_dir()` prints the folder path. 

On a cluster, we recommend setting the reference folder somowhere other than your
home directory where disk quotas are lower: see [Disk space, caches, and offline use](Caches-and-Offline.html).
